question: in our deployment setting (monocular RGB video, static camera, fixed intrinsics, offline access to the whole video), how much does using more frames improve single-frame calibration, and what part of the error can more frames never remove

aggregation_unit.rule: frames are NEVER pooled across sequences, even when the same physical camera id reappears, because a deployment estimates the calibration of one video
aggregation_unit.cross_sequence_repeats: may be used for diagnostics only, never as aggregation input

data.hand_quality: NOT used as a filter - hand REVIEW/EXCLUDE labels never remove a camera-valid view

phase_a.inference: NONE - reuses CAM-EXP-003 / 003.1 per-frame predictions verbatim
phase_a.subsets: ALL C(8,N) subsets are evaluated (8, 28, 70, 1) so no result depends on which frames a single random draw picked
phase_a.statistical_unit: the view. Subsets are collapsed to the view's expected error first; the ~19k subsets are never treated as independent samples
excluded: GT-undistorted images (CAM-EXP-003.1 condition C) - oracle, not deployable
PF-centered + GT-undistorted - measured to degrade in CAM-EXP-003.1

aggregation_methods.geomean: exp(mean(log f)) - focal error is multiplicative, so the log domain is analysed too
aggregation_methods.log_huber: Huber M-estimator of location in log space, iteratively reweighted, scale = MAD/0.6745, tuning constant c = 1.345 (the standard robust-statistics default for 95% Gaussian efficiency). NOT tuned against GT.

ensembles.constraint: parameter-free and GT-blind only. Fitting or tuning ensemble weights against this dataset's GT is forbidden in this experiment.
ensembles.E1_perframe_mean: per-frame arithmetic mean of the two focals, then median over frames
ensembles.E2_perframe_geomean: per-frame geometric mean, then median over frames
ensembles.E3_perview_mean: median over frames per model, then arithmetic mean of the two
ensembles.E4_perview_geomean: median over frames per model, then geometric mean of the two
ensembles.E5_three_model_median: median over frames per model, then median across the three models

oracle.ORACLE_BEST_OF_N: the single frame inside the subset with the smallest GT focal error
oracle.status: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY - uses GT, is not a method, and is never mixed with deployable numbers

bias_noise_decomposition.identity: mean(e^2) = mean(b^2) + mean(r^2) exactly, since residuals are zero-mean within each view
bias_noise_decomposition.reported: each term as a fraction of the total squared log error

phase_b_stopping_rule.criterion_A: median relative focal error drops by >= 10 % relative
phase_b_stopping_rule.criterion_B: within-5 % rate increases by >= 3 absolute percentage points
phase_b_stopping_rule.action_otherwise: record SATURATED_BY_8_FRAMES and skip PHASE B

forbidden: choosing frames using scene heuristics (lines, clutter, hand visibility)
frame_selection.note: scene-aware selection is deferred to CAM-EXP-005+

metrics: identical definitions to CAM-EXP-003: relative focal error = |f_pred - f_gt| / f_gt * 100
depth_reference: CAM-EXP-002 sensitivity (5 % ~ 32.8 mm, 10 % ~ 65.6 mm, 20 % ~ 131.2 mm isolated depth displacement) is quoted only as an interpretation reference. Nothing here measures depth.
out_of_scope: hand geometry as a calibration cue
